spoken_phrase: Why do astronauts grow taller in space?
ideal_footage: Astronaut full body or medical body measurement before or after spaceflight
fallback_footage: Astronaut standing or moving inside a spacecraft

spoken_phrase: On Earth, gravity constantly compresses your spine. In microgravity, that pressure disappears.
ideal_footage: Astronaut visibly floating in microgravity inside the ISS
fallback_footage: Astronaut moving weightlessly through an ISS module

spoken_phrase: Your spine stretches, and the discs between your vertebrae expand.
ideal_footage: Astronaut undergoing ultrasound or human physiology research aboard ISS
fallback_footage: Astronaut participating in human body research aboard ISS

spoken_phrase: Astronauts can grow up to three percent taller.
ideal_footage: Astronaut body measurement or medical examination connected to spaceflight

spoken_phrase: But back on Earth, gravity compresses the spine again, and the extra height disappears.
ideal_footage: Astronaut immediately after landing or during postflight recovery
fallback_footage: Astronaut exercising or rehabilitating after spaceflight
